findings.F1: Among the 10-day grid cases in a choppy, calm market, the 30-day return ranks with the next 10 days' return over the coin's drift (Spearman 0.42, p 0.0002, 76 cases); cases after a month rise ended +9.9 % over drift (39) and cases after a month fall ended −4.0 % (37). The signed gain over 31 days has a t of only 1.38, so the ranking is clearer than the mean.
findings.F2: The choppy, agitated cases are too few to read (20 cases, 13 days, rho 0.34, p 0.14). Over all recorded chop-regime grid cases the 30-day return still ranks with the next 10 days (Spearman 0.18, p 0.013, 198 cases). The two lowest month quintiles were followed by −6.9 % and −5.3 % over drift, and the highest quintile by +7.3 % (t −1.44, −1.94 and +0.89 over 22 to 31 days).
findings.F3: The tested book is a short whose gains and losses come from the coin's own large moves. Its worst 1 % of days (124) came with the coin up +11.9 % and lost −5.6 % each, and its best 1 % came with the coin down −10.2 % and gained +5.5 % each. Each tail alone is about 24 times the book's net total, and the net yearly return is +0.0 % over 7.94 years. The short side also fights a −1.50 % normal drift per case, which turns the unusual move of +1.40 % (t 2.08) into a total move of −0.10 %, below the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F4: In a falling, calm market the 30-day move also continues over the next 10 days (Spearman 0.21, p 0.03, 107 cases). Cases after a month fall ended −3.7 % over drift (81) and cases after a rise ended +2.4 % (26), with a signed t of 2.15 over 30 days. In a falling, agitated market the month move instead reverses (Spearman −0.21, p 0.01, 146 cases).
findings.F5: A one-day fall large against the coin's 30-day swing is followed by a next-day gain only in agitated markets. The lowest seventh (mean z −1.44) was followed by +1.19 % over drift (t 2.26, 231 days) when agitated and by +0.32 % (t 0.87, 238 days) when calm. The ranking of falls against the next day was negative in every year from 2018 to 2021 (rho −0.06 to −0.12). This is the agitated fall rebound the map already holds in 16 falling-agitated long strategies, so it is no discovery.
findings.F6: The weekday effects in coin returns disappear once cases on the same day are counted as one: the next-day excess by weekday has a t between −1.07 and 1.47 over about 206 days each. The pattern of short-term volatility expansion (10-day against 30-day swing) is not monotone across quintiles (t from −1.61 to 1.45), so neither is a finding.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the larger a coin's 30-day return is in either direction, the further it moves the same way over the next 10 days, so that a stronger month rise is followed by a larger rise and a deeper month fall by a larger fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a flat, quiet two-month market follows the coin's month move both ways, scaling the position with the month's size, and takes the long side, where the coin's drift helps, as well as the short.
ideas.name: choppy calm month continuation

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the deeper a coin's fall over the past 30 days, the more it keeps falling over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts a coin sliding quietly in a falling market in proportion to the month's fall, rather than buying it as an agitated fall would invite.
ideas.name: falling calm slide continues
